headline: Mortgages are 9.8% of accounts but 52% of exposure, and default most
evidence: Mortgage default rate 24.7% (n=1,432) vs 16.1% portfolio; 65% of all defaulted exposure ($82.6M of $126.9M). Value-weighted default rate is 21.1% against 16.1% by count.
so_what: Headline default rate understates dollar risk. Mortgage underwriting, LTV limits and early-arrears monitoring are the highest-leverage controls; report the exposure-weighted rate alongside the count-based one.

headline: Unemployed borrowers default at 35%, and low income compounds it
evidence: Unemployed: 35.0% (n=718, 4.9% of accounts). Income <40k: unemployed 41.7% (n=350) vs salaried 23.9% (n=314); 40-60k: 31.0% (n=197) vs 21.2% (n=1061). Across all employment, <40k income defaults at 32.4% vs 9.5% at 100k+.
so_what: Employment status adds risk on top of income, so an income-only cut-off misses it. Consider a stricter policy (co-borrower, lower limit, collateral) for unemployed applicants rather than a flat income threshold.

headline: Delinquency is a steep early-warning ladder: 8% -> 29% default
evidence: 0 late/missed months: 8.1% (n=2,153); 1: 12.4%; 2-3: 17.1%; 4+: 28.7% (n=2,043, 13.9% of accounts). Already by months 1-6, 2+ delinquent months means 23.2% vs 13.7%.
so_what: Risk is visible within six months of origination. Trigger collections outreach after the second delinquent month instead of waiting for deep arrears; this is also the basis of the dashboard's anomaly review queue.

headline: A written-off line elsewhere lifts default from 14.6% to 18.7%, most on Business Loans
evidence: 29% of accounts (n=4,279) belong to customers with a written-off bureau line. Largest gap on Business Loan: 20.2% vs 14.5%. Thin-file customers: 17.6% (n=1,462).
so_what: External write-offs are a cheap, reliable screen that should tighten limits or pricing, especially on unsecured business and card lending; thin-file customers sit above average and deserve manual review rather than a default 'clean' assumption.

headline: Geography and channel barely move risk; age and income do
evidence: Region range 15.0%-16.9%, city tier 15.5%-16.4%, channel 15.4%-16.9%. By age: <30 defaults at 21.6% (n=3,250) vs 13.8% for 40-49 and 6.8% for 60+ (n=368).
so_what: Regional or channel tightening would cost volume without reducing risk. Focus policy on borrower attributes (income, employment, bureau history) and product mix. Treat age as a monitoring variable only, subject to fair-lending review.
